title: Binary Treatment: Average Treatment Effect
text: vignette demonstrates frengression binary treatment data. estimate Average Treatment Effect (ATE) compare simple doubly-robust estimator.

title: Binary Treatment: Average Treatment Effect
text: Z∼N(0,1)Z \sim N(0, 1) X∼Bernoulli(logit−1(Z))X \sim \text{Bernoulli}(\text{logit}^{-1}(Z)) (confounded treatment) Y=2X+Z+εY = 2X + Z + \varepsilon, ε∼N(0,0.52)\varepsilon \sim N(0, 0.5^2) True ATE = E[Y|(X=1)]−E[Y|(X=0)]=2E[Y|(X=1)] - E[Y|(X=0)] = 2.
code:
library(Rfrengression) set.seed(123)  n <- 3000 z <- matrix(rnorm(n), ncol = 1) prob_x <- plogis(z) x <- matrix(rbinom(n, 1, prob_x), ncol = 1) y <- 2 * x + z + matrix(rnorm(n, sd = 0.5), ncol = 1)  cat("Treatment prevalence:", mean(x), "
") #> Treatment prevalence: 0.5066667 cat("Naive difference-in-means:", mean(y[x == 1]) - mean(y[x == 0]), "
") #> Naive difference-in-means: 2.853061 cat("(biased due to confounding)
") #> (biased due to confounding)

title: Binary Treatment: Average Treatment Effect
code: model <- frengression(x_dim = 1, y_dim = 1, z_dim = 1,                       x_binary = TRUE, noise_dim = 5)  model <- train_y(model, x, z, y, num_iters = 500, lr = 1e-3,                  print_every = 100) model <- train_xz(model, x, z, num_iters = 500, lr = 1e-4,                    print_every = 100)

title: Binary Treatment: Average Treatment Effect
code: # E[Y | do(X=1)] y1 <- predict(model, matrix(1, ncol = 1), type = "mean", nsample = 1000) # E[Y | do(X=0)] y0 <- predict(model, matrix(0, ncol = 1), type = "mean", nsample = 1000)  ate_freng <- y1 - y0 cat("Frengression ATE estimate:", ate_freng, "\n") cat("True ATE: 2\n")

title: Binary Treatment: Average Treatment Effect
code: # Simple DR estimator for comparison # Convert matrix columns to vectors for lm/glm xv <- as.numeric(x) yv <- as.numeric(y) zv <- as.numeric(z)  e_hat <- glm(xv ~ zv, family = binomial)$fitted.values mu1_hat <- predict(lm(yv ~ zv, subset = xv == 1), newdata = data.frame(zv = zv)) mu0_hat <- predict(lm(yv ~ zv, subset = xv == 0), newdata = data.frame(zv = zv))  dr_ate <- mean(mu1_hat - mu0_hat +                xv * (yv - mu1_hat) / e_hat -                (1 - xv) * (yv - mu0_hat) / (1 - e_hat)) cat("Doubly-robust ATE estimate:", dr_ate, "\n")

title: Continuous Treatment: Average Dose-Response Function
text: vignette demonstrates frengression continuous treatment data. generate synthetic data known causal effect (ADRF), train frengression model, verify recovers true dose-response curve.

title: Continuous Treatment: Average Dose-Response Function
text: DGP confounder Z affects treatment X outcome Y: Z∼N(0,1)Z \sim N(0, 1) X=Z+εXX = Z + \varepsilon_X, εX∼N(0,0.52)\varepsilon_X \sim N(0, 0.5^2) Y=2X+Z2+εYY = 2X + Z^2 + \varepsilon_Y, εY∼N(0,0.52)\varepsilon_Y \sim N(0, 0.5^2) true ADRF E[Y|(X=x)]=2x+E[Z2]=2x+1E[Y | (X=x)] = 2x + E[Z^2] = 2x + 1.
code: library(Rfrengression) set.seed(42)  n <- 2000 z <- matrix(rnorm(n), ncol = 1) x <- z + matrix(rnorm(n, sd = 0.5), ncol = 1) y <- 2 * x + z^2 + matrix(rnorm(n, sd = 0.5), ncol = 1)

title: Continuous Treatment: Average Dose-Response Function
text: Training two-stage: first outcome model (model_y + model_eta), marginal model (model_xz).
code: model <- frengression(x_dim = 1, y_dim = 1, z_dim = 1, noise_dim = 5)  # Stage 1: Train outcome model model <- train_y(model, x, z, y, num_iters = 500, lr = 1e-3,                  print_every = 100)  # Stage 2: Train marginal model model <- train_xz(model, x, z, num_iters = 500, lr = 1e-4,                    print_every = 100)  print(model)

title: Continuous Treatment: Average Dose-Response Function
text: evaluate causal effect grid treatment values:
code: x_grid <- matrix(seq(-3, 3, length.out = 50), ncol = 1) y_pred <- predict(model, x_grid, type = "mean", nsample = 500)  # True ADRF y_true <- 2 * x_grid + 1  # Quantile bands y_quant <- predict(model, x_grid, type = "quantile", nsample = 500,                    quantiles = c(0.1, 0.9))

title: Specifying Custom Causal Margins
text: key feature frengression specify_causal(): can replace learned causal margin user-defined function. allows generating joint data (X, Y, Z) causal mechanism Y|(X) exactly specify, preserving learned marginal P(X, Z) confounding structure. useful benchmarking causal inference methods controlled ground truth.

title: Specifying Custom Causal Margins
code: library(Rfrengression) set.seed(42)  n <- 2000 z <- matrix(rnorm(n), ncol = 1) x <- z + matrix(rnorm(n, sd = 0.5), ncol = 1) y <- 2 * x + z^2 + matrix(rnorm(n, sd = 0.5), ncol = 1) model <- frengression(x_dim = 1, y_dim = 1, z_dim = 1, noise_dim = 5) model <- train_y(model, x, z, y, num_iters = 300, lr = 1e-3,                  print_every = 100, silent = TRUE) model <- train_xz(model, x, z, num_iters = 300, lr = 1e-4,                    print_every = 100, silent = TRUE)

title: Specifying Custom Causal Margins
text: causal function takes (x, eta) eta ~ N(0, ):
code: # Causal margin 1: Linear Y = 5X + noise model_linear <- specify_causal(model, function(x, eta) 5 * x + eta)  # Causal margin 2: Quadratic Y = X^2 + 0.5*noise model_quad <- specify_causal(model, function(x, eta) x^2 + 0.5 * eta)  # Causal margin 3: Heterogeneous effect model_hetero <- specify_causal(model, function(x, eta) {   torch::torch_where(x > 0, 3 * x + eta, -x + 0.5 * eta) })

what: Step 3: Generate Joint Data with Each Margin
title: Specifying Custom Causal Margins
code:
joint_linear <- sample_joint(model_linear, sample_size = 1000) joint_quad <- sample_joint(model_quad, sample_size = 1000) joint_hetero <- sample_joint(model_hetero, sample_size = 1000)  cat("All share the same marginal P(X,Z):
") cat("  Linear:  mean(X) =", round(mean(joint_linear$x), 2),     " mean(Z) =", round(mean(joint_linear$z), 2), "
") cat("  Quad:    mean(X) =", round(mean(joint_quad$x), 2),     " mean(Z) =", round(mean(joint_quad$z), 2), "
") cat("  Hetero:  mean(X) =", round(mean(joint_hetero$x), 2),     " mean(Z) =", round(mean(joint_hetero$z), 2), "
")

title: Specifying Custom Causal Margins
code: x_grid <- matrix(seq(-3, 3, length.out = 50), ncol = 1)  # Sample causal margin for each model y_lin <- predict(model_linear, x_grid, type = "mean", nsample = 300) y_quad <- predict(model_quad, x_grid, type = "mean", nsample = 300) y_het <- predict(model_hetero, x_grid, type = "mean", nsample = 300) par(mfrow = c(1, 3))  plot(x_grid, y_lin, type = "l", lwd = 2, col = "blue",      main = "Linear: Y = 5X + noise", xlab = "X", ylab = "E[Y|do(X)]") lines(x_grid, 5 * x_grid, lty = 2, col = "red", lwd = 2) legend("topleft", c("Estimated", "True"), col = c("blue", "red"), lty = 1:2)  plot(x_grid, y_quad, type = "l", lwd = 2, col = "blue",      main = "Quadratic: Y = X^2 + noise", xlab = "X", ylab = "E[Y|do(X)]") lines(x_grid, x_grid^2, lty = 2, col = "red", lwd = 2) legend("topleft", c("Estimated", "True"), col = c("blue", "red"), lty = 1:2)  plot(x_grid, y_het, type = "l", lwd = 2, col = "blue",      main = "Heterogeneous effect", xlab = "X", ylab = "E[Y|do(X)]") true_het <- ifelse(x_grid > 0, 3 * x_grid, -x_grid) lines(x_grid, true_het, lty = 2, col = "red", lwd = 2) legend("topleft", c("Estimated", "True"), col = c("blue", "red"), lty = 1:2)  par(mfrow = c(1, 1))

title: Longitudinal Data with FrengressionSeq
text: frengression_seq() extends base model time-varying (longitudinal) data. maintains separate networks time step, modeling sequential dependencies: S→(X0,Z0)→(X1,Z1)→⋯S \(X_0, Z_0) \(X_1, Z_1) \\cdots.

title: Longitudinal Data with FrengressionSeq
text: generate 3-step longitudinal data : SS: binary baseline covariate XtX_t: binary treatment time tt ZtZ_t: continuous time-varying confounder YtY_t: binary outcome time tt
code: library(Rfrengression) set.seed(42)  n <- 3000 T_steps <- 3  # Baseline s <- matrix(rbinom(n, 1, 0.5), ncol = 1)  # Pre-allocate x_all <- matrix(0, n, T_steps) z_all <- matrix(0, n, T_steps) y_all <- matrix(0, n, T_steps)  # Time 0 z_all[, 1] <- rnorm(n, mean = 0.3 * s) x_all[, 1] <- rbinom(n, 1, plogis(0.5 * z_all[, 1] + 0.2 * s)) y_all[, 1] <- rbinom(n, 1, plogis(-2 + 0.5 * x_all[, 1] + 0.3 * z_all[, 1]))  # Time 1 and 2 for (t in 2:T_steps) {   z_all[, t] <- rnorm(n, mean = 0.3 * s + 0.2 * z_all[, t - 1])   x_all[, t] <- rbinom(n, 1, plogis(0.5 * z_all[, t] + 0.2 * s))   y_all[, t] <- rbinom(n, 1, plogis(-2 + 0.5 * x_all[, t] +                                         0.3 * z_all[, t] + 0.1 * x_all[, t - 1])) }  cat("Event rates per time step:", colMeans(y_all), "\n") #> Event rates per time step: 0.16 0.172 0.189 cat("Treatment rates per time step:", colMeans(x_all), "\n") #> Treatment rates per time step: 0.5313333 0.5453333 0.5473333

title: Longitudinal Data with FrengressionSeq
text: Training three stages: (1) train_xz, (2) train_e, (3) train_y.
code: model <- frengression_seq(   x_dim = 1, y_dim = 1, z_dim = 1,   T_steps = 3, s_dim = 1,   noise_dim = 5, num_layer = 3, hidden_dim = 50,   x_binary = TRUE, y_binary = TRUE,   s_in_predict = TRUE )  print(model)  # Stage 1: Marginal (X, Z) model model <- train_xz(model, s = s, x = x_all, z = z_all,                    num_iters = 500, lr = 1e-4, print_every = 100)  # Stage 2: Confounder model E model <- train_e(model, s = s, x = x_all, z = z_all,                   num_iters = 500, lr = 1e-4, print_every = 100)  # Stage 3: Outcome model Y model <- train_y(model, s = s, x = x_all, z = z_all, y = y_all,                   num_iters = 500, lr = 1e-4, print_every = 100)

what: Counterfactual: Always Treated vs Never Treated
title: Longitudinal Data with FrengressionSeq
code:
# Predict under always-treated and never-treated regimes s_test <- matrix(rep(c(0, 1), each = 500), ncol = 1)  x_always <- matrix(1, nrow = nrow(s_test), ncol = T_steps) x_never <- matrix(0, nrow = nrow(s_test), ncol = T_steps)  y_always <- predict_causal(model, s = s_test, x = x_always,                             target = "mean", sample_size = 200) y_never <- predict_causal(model, s = s_test, x = x_never,                            target = "mean", sample_size = 200)  cat("
E[Y_t | do(X=always 1)] per time step:
") for (t in seq_len(T_steps)) cat("  t =", t, ":", mean(y_always[[t]]), "
") cat("E[Y_t | do(X=always 0)] per time step:
") for (t in seq_len(T_steps)) cat("  t =", t, ":", mean(y_never[[t]]), "
") ate_t <- sapply(seq_len(T_steps), function(t) {   mean(y_always[[t]]) - mean(y_never[[t]]) })  plot(1:T_steps, ate_t, type = "b", pch = 19, lwd = 2,      xlab = "Time Step", ylab = "ATE",      main = "Time-Varying Average Treatment Effect") abline(h = 0, lty = 2, col = "gray")
